Welcome from the Head
A very warm welcome to Tiffin School.
We are a State School for boys in Years 7-11 and with a fully co-educational Sixth Form.
Our students tell me how they feel a strong sense of belonging to the school community and value their teachers and their excellent teaching; and the extraordinary breadth of co-curricular opportunities. The students are supported by our outstanding staff, and their own peers, in developing as people who are happy, kind, reflective, proactive and successful. I hope that our website helps bring to life what we value most at Tiffin School, and the rich education our students enjoy.
Explore Tiffin School
To prepare our students for their future lives in the modern world, we aim to nurture a love of learning and the pursuit of academic excellence and scholarship. Tiffinians are encouraged to develop independence, adaptability, determination and confidence.

At Tiffin, we believe that education is about developing the whole person, and we provide the opportunities and encouragement for students to engage in a quite extraordinary range of activities that will encourage and cultivate commitment, leadership, teamwork, initiative, responsibility and confidence.

Welcome from the Head
Welcome to Tiffin School, one of the UK’s leading State Grammar Schools.
At the heart of what makes Tiffin special is the strong sense of community. Although a large school of 1500 students, we maintain a family feel in which students are valued as individuals and have a strong sense of belonging to their form, house, year group and the school. Academic standards are very high, and yet we celebrate so much more than just results. Students engage in learning outside the classroom through a vast number of clubs and societies. The co-curricular depth and breadth is unmatched for a state school, and all this is made possible through a highly motivated and committed staff body. We now welcome girls in the Sixth Form, helping make Tiffin a diverse and vibrant community in which students thrive and maintain a strong attachment to the school for the rest of their lives.
I hope this website gives you some insight into what makes Tiffin an exceptional school.
Garth Williams Headteacher

Our Purpose
Our guiding principle is that actions are a true mark of character.
Here, belonging is a way of life, where regardless of background or belief, we cherish everyone for who they are and help them to thrive and flourish. Here, we foster curiosity, spark creativity and cultivate a love of learning. And here, we make a positive difference to the world around us by giving back to our community, giving support to each other and giving our best in all we do.
This is an outstanding school that believes in doing what’s right, not what’s easy, and where we empower remarkable people with an education that touches hearts, inspires minds and nurtures generosity.
This is Tiffin. Where acting with integrity speaks volumes.
Our Values
Tiffin School Values are underpinned by the Fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. Together, these values help to create a respectful, inclusive and supportive school community in which every pupil can thrive.
Our Vision
Inclusive Excellence and Shared Success
By 2030, our provision will set the standard for inclusive excellence and shared success, with every student achieving and thriving, prepared to lead and give back to their world.
Below are some examples of how we are already making progress towards reaching this ambition.
Discover more about our vision and the steps we are taking to achieve it here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tiffin School Strong Performances for Tiffin Run Club - Tiffin School
pageCache.text:
Search this Site:
After a great success at Skinner’s last week, the run club team traveled down to the southeast for Year 9 and below relays. The venue was a sun-blessed Guildford Grammar School sports field in Shalford.
Without the Stella Year 10s, there was a huge step up from the rest of the club. Dylan K blasted off the start to good effect, placing us in easily the top dozen of the field. Max C took up the baton and forged up to the top 10. Fresh from bronze success, Angus F forged further up the field of 70 teams. He was again well within the top 3 in years 7 and 8s on show, though a year 7 athlete himself. Bardy W clocked the fastest Tiffin time of the day and blasted us up to a very fine 4th position. Clocking up the only Tiffin sub-8 min time for the 2.2K double-lap course in the process.
The B team did well in their class. Again in the top 5 of all B teams. Joshua H, F Arthur A, Karam A, and Oscar L combined well in this respect. The C team did even better, being in the top 3 in their section. Oscar L, Casper V and Atticus V, and Maxim C did well here, especially as ¾ of the team had their debut for the school.

Ofsted Report
Tiffin School is highly acclaimed for consistently achieving outstanding academic results, whilst also providing an extraordinary range of co-curricular activities, as we aim to develop the all-round attributes of the young people we nurture. Indeed, the results in 2023 were well above the national average and our students also won a record number of 34 places at Oxbridge.
Ofsted came to the School in May 2022, to inspect us under their new framework. They visited whilst Years 11 & 13 were on study leave, and all other year groups except Year 10 were on our internal exams week.
Consequently, they were only able to visit a tiny handful of lessons in just one year group, and did not see the usual rich co-curricular programme. They also had no public exam results to base any judgements on. It was therefore not a normal time to inspect a school. Their report is here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tiffin School Tiffin Boys' Choir and Girls' Choir Perform at the Royal Festival Hall - Tiffin School
pageCache.text:
Search this Site:
It was another exceptional week for Tiffin’s musicians, with members of the Tiffin Boys’ Choir and Tiffin Girls’ Choir performing Benjamin Britten’s monumental War Requiem at the Royal Festival Hall.
Under the direction of James Day, our singers joined the London Philharmonic Orchestra, London Philharmonic Choir and London Symphony Chorus for this extraordinary work, conducted by Edward Gardner. Britten’s War Requiem is one of the most powerful large-scale choral works of the twentieth century, bringing together the traditional Latin Requiem with the moving poetry of First World War poet Wilfred Owen.
The scale of the performance was immense, requiring three choirs, two orchestras and three internationally renowned soloists, and it was a remarkable opportunity for our students to perform alongside some of the country’s finest professional musicians and singers on one of London’s great concert stages.
The performance received an outstanding reception, with the audience held in silence at its conclusion before responding with thunderous applause. Experiences of this calibre demonstrate the extraordinary opportunities available to Tiffin students and the remarkable standard of our choral tradition.
Huge congratulations to all the students involved and, in particular, to James Day and the Music Department for their continued dedication in making opportunities such as this possible.

Tiffin School's Careers Programme
Tiffin School is committed to providing a high quality careers and progression programme, and excellent support to our students. In line with Government guidance, we utilise the Gatsby benchmarks to develop our careers programme.
Through timetabled lessons, tutor time sessions, use of PDD days, trips and visits, individual meetings and off-timetable activities, we aim to open our students’ minds to a wide variety of career paths, to challenge their thinking and preconceived ideas on pathways and careers, to encourage their aspirations, and to give them tailored and relevant information and advice.
Our careers and progression programme, which you can view below, is designed so that students can begin to learn how to navigate and manage their future. This includes becoming more aware of their strengths, values and interests, learning about many different areas of work and pathways, understanding how to keep options open, building experience, valuing how their lessons and other activities contribute to their future, and developing career management skills.
We have recently introduced the Unifrog platform to sit at the heart of our careers programme. Students can use this to log and reflect on activities and placements, and to explore and research careers and progression pathways. This is also used as part of our 6 PDD ‘Beyond Tiffin Life’ work booklets for each year group.
Careers News (for all students), Y12 and Y13 Progression Bulletins are weekly sources of external opportunities, ideas and events, including employer insight events, university tasters and work experience opportunities. We invite alumni and other contacts in to talk to students about their careers, and our older year groups share their experience with the years below. Our academic departments and the careers and progression team look for opportunities for students to explore pathways and experience the world of work. Recent examples include: Young Reporter, Advertising Unlocked, Young Enterprise and a Study Abroad series.
Mr D Ryde (L7 Careers Adviser), is our Careers Leader and has the role of Head of Careers; managing the careers programme and providing independent and impartial guidance for all year groups. Our Senior Leader link is Mr. A Dean. Our Governor responsible for Careers is Mrs A Jones.
Mr Ryde is the first point of contact for any questions or proposals about our careers programme. Parents, employers or education/training providers can contact him on 020 8546 4638 or careers@tiffin.kingston.sch.uk. Pupils can get in touch via the same email address or drop in to the careers office (Room 108C), at school.

Tiffin School Alumni
Community is an incredibly important part of life at all stages – offering support, sharing knowledge and providing a sense of belonging. Tiffin students spend years as a part of the Tiffin School community as a pupil and that doesn’t change when they walk through the school gates for a final time. Upon leaving, they automatically become a part of our Alumni community.
Alumni receive a termly newsletter keeping them up to date with Tiffin life and news from fellow Old Tiffinians and the School holds a variety of Alumni events throughout the year including a carol service in central London at Christmas, summer drinks in the Head’s Garden and online career events throughout the year.
Our new online community portal offers Alumni the chance to keep in touch with the School and each other – simply click the button below to create your online profile.
For many years, the generosity of Alumni has helped us to provide a wide range of opportunities and activities to broaden and enrich the education of Tiffin students. From the performing arts to the sports field, in the classroom and beyond, the Tiffin Education Fund* has been the cornerstone of the provision of an outstanding all round education.
Every contribution increases the opportunities Tiffin is able to offer students – click here to support Tiffin students now and in future.

Tiffin Education Fund
Over many years the generosity of parents and Alumni has helped us provide a wide range of opportunities and activities for all students to broaden and enrich their education. From the performing arts to the sports field, in the classroom and beyond, the Tiffin Education Fund has been the cornerstone of the provision of an outstanding education. Parental and Alumni contributions have proved vital in sustaining an education provision that remains uniquely diverse and of a high standard to benefit all students.
The Tiffin Education Fund contributes to our building improvement plan and the enhancement of the learning environment of our School. The new Sports Centre Extension, the Dining Hall and the new Sixth Form Centre are examples of such projects. Further developments have included the updating of our laboratories, the MUGA, the cricket nets and the refurbishment of the facilities in the School Hall which has helped to support drama, music and House activities. This much improved environment benefits all students, whatever their interests.
Tiffin students benefit hugely from the Tiffin Education Fund supporting a comprehensive programme of wider opportunities including sports, music and performing arts. Whatever a student’s choice from our wider opportunities programme, the Fund is there to provide a rich menu of activities to carry them forward in their education and enhance their enjoyment of life at Tiffin School.
The Tiffin Education Fund helps us to extend the academic programme within the School. Not only are we able to offer a wider curriculum and additional learning resources, the Fund helps us to to constantly improve our ICT infrastructure and provide staff to support learning where needed.
Make a Contribution
The current suggested contribution for current Tiffin families is £520 per year, per child. This amounts to £10 per week, and we believe that there is no better way to help a child’s education than this. Many families support at a higher level than this already and others are contributing what they can. It is all appreciated equally and the benefits are immense. Regular monthly payments, such as those made by direct debit, help the School to plan more efficiently.
If you wish to talk about a donation to the School, please contact the Development Office on 020 8546 4638 or via email at development@tiffin.kingston.sch.uk.
The Tiffin Education Fund is a fund held within The Tiffin School Foundation (registered charity number 1185240) which has been set up to ensure that your voluntary contributions benefit every student in some way.

Find Us
Tiffin is located on Queen Elizabeth Road, with the main pedestrian entrance on its junction with Birkenhead Avenue. We are a short walk from Kingston Town Centre and within easy reach of various public transport stops.
Grists Sport Ground
Games afternoons, rugby and cricket matches are played at our sports fields, Grists, located on Summer Road, East Molesey, KT8 9LS.
Please note: Opposition buses travelling to Grists should not enter Summer Road, but pick up and drop off in the lay by on Hampton Court Way.
Grists is a dog-free zone; no dogs are permitted anywhere on the site.
Travelling to Tiffin
The post code for Sat Nav use is KT2 6RL (full address at the bottom of the page). Please note, there is no visitor parking at the main school site.
We have a designated disabled parking space available upon request; if you have any access requirements, please contact the main office to discuss these.
The nearest mainline rail station is Kingston (operated by South West Trains, zone 6), which is a five-minute walk from the School. There are regular services to and from London Waterloo via Clapham Junction and Wimbledon. Upon exiting the station, turn left and walk past Tesco and the bus garage. follow the road round to the right and you will see Tiffin on your left.
Tiffin is well-served by a number of bus routes. The following stop within a couple of minutes’ walk:

We are so grateful to the Tiffin community for supporting us to build and furnish our fantastic, modern facility for the Tiffin Sixth Form.

The new Sixth Form Centre is also equipped with specialised facilities which creates an environment conducive to advanced learning, helping our exceptional students make the most of their time at Tiffin.

Many thanks to the Tiffin Community, for their donations enabling us to complete the wonderful facilities for the teaching of sport and fitness at Tiffin School. We have replaced the battered 1940s war-time ammunition store, which used to serve as a gym, with a modern gym, two fitness suites, changing areas and office space.
The building was officially declared open by Alec Stewart OBE, former Tiffin Pupil and former England and Surrey Cricket Captain. Due to Covid restrictions it was not possible to have a public opening, but if you click this link you will see a video of the event, filmed by some of our students.

I am delighted that, through the generosity of the Tiffin Community, we received enough donations to complete the building and it is now a vibrant part of the School. We have replaced the 1948 pre-cast concrete canteen with a superb kitchen and dining area, five additional classrooms and office spaces.

Welcome from the Chair
The School is rapidly nearing its 150th anniversary in 2030. The Governing Board of Tiffin School is responsible for the strategic oversight of the School, its vision, ethos, values and longer-term priorities. It oversees the School’s educational provision and outcomes, the welfare of its students and staff, and its financial affairs. The Governors are volunteers who give their time and expertise freely for the benefit of the School. Many of them are alumni, parents, and former parents, and are closely linked to Tiffin in some way. Others are carefully chosen external professionals with needed specialist skills in education and business.
Exam results in the summer of 2026 were once again excellent at A Level ( 93% A*AB, 71% A*A and 38% A*). Most graduating Tiffinians from the Class of 2026 went on to universities of their first choice including 38 offers for Oxbridge places. We wish them all well in the next stage of their education. The 2026 GCSE results were also truly outstanding and also our best ever with 88% at grades 9-7, 72% at grades 9-8, and 44% at grade 9. The Governors’ congratulations go out to all the students who have achieved these wonderful results and of course to all the Tiffin staff who guided them there.
The continuing attraction of Tiffin School was once again demonstrated by the very strong demand for entry in September 2026 from external candidates at both Years 7 and 12. It was particularly pleasing to see the admission of another large cohort of nearly 100 female students into the Sixth Form.
The sports facilities at the School premises in Kingston were transformed in 2026 with the completion of a second all-weather pitch, a new netball court, upgraded cricket nets, a new long jump pit and the refurbishment of the first all-weather pitch. These facilities will be enjoyed by generations of Tiffinians to come. We are very grateful to the support of alumni and parents and the legacy of a former teacher for most of the required funding. The Governors’ heartfelt thanks go to all who have supported the fundraising. Importantly, two very significant grants from the DfE to upgrade fire safety and replace a boiler were successfully bid for by the School in competition with other schools. Much of the work has been completed during the summer of 2026.
The coming year will see a continued focus by the School’s Senior Leadership Team and staff, led by the Headteacher, Garth Williams, on making further school improvements. Built on the bedrock of our School values (belonging, learning and giving) and under the overall 5 year (2025-30) vision of ‘inclusive excellence and shared success’ the School will have a particular focus during the 2026-27 academic year on the curriculum, tutoring, and student participation. A major concern will be finalising plans for the development of our Grists playing fields and pavilions and sourcing the needed funding. The School and The Tiffin School Foundation, the charity which now owns both the School land in Kingston and our playing fields at Grists, hope to finalise amended development plans during the 2026-27 academic year to be presented for planning approval.
It is an honour to serve with the other Governors and Trustees at Tiffin and to be an alumnus of this great School. We are very proud of recent national recognition in league tables published in August ‘26 – Tiffin were 5th in the ‘Daily Telegraphs’ ‘Best Sixth Form’ table; and 3rd in ‘The Spectators’ Oxbridge Offer table. We will continue to strive to provide the very best possible teaching and learning environment, extra-curricular experience and facilities for our students and staff.

After graduating with a degree in Economics, Jane enjoyed a successful career in business before entering the teaching profession in 2000. From 2010-2024 she held senior leadership positions in schools including two Headships of selective schools and she was also the founding CEO of the Girls’ Learning Trust, growing the multi-academy trust to three schools during her tenure.
Jane was also a governor at Royal Russell School in Croydon from 2015-2019, was joint-President of the Association of State Girls’ Schools from 2017-2019 and has also served on the Girls’ School Association Education Committee from 2022-2024.
Since retiring from headship in August 2024, Jane holds several roles alongside her position at Tiffin. These include being a member of the Education Committee of the Worshipful Company of Haberdashers, Chair of the Resources Committee at Sutton Tuition and Reintegration Service (STARS) and a trustee of the Russell School Trust.

I am the Chair of the Admissions Committee and a member of the Resources Committee, Education Committee, and Head’s Performance Review Group.
There has been tremendous change at the School. In strategic matters, as Chair, I worked with other governors on the academy conversion in 2011, the appointments of a new Headteacher in both 2014 and 2022, the change to a mixed 6th form in 2019 and more recently on securing the strategic future of Grist’s. I have been involved in the successful funding and construction of major site improvements including our new classroom, kitchen, and dining facility in 2018, the new gym extension in 2020, the 2022 LRC infill project and the MUGA2 project. It is an absolute privilege to serve as a governor of this great School.

A well-rounded education which challenges the individual is essential in today’s competitive work environment, whatever path they choose to follow in the future. Both my son and daughter were fortunate to attend Tiffin School and Tiffin Girls School respectively. They benefitted from a great all-round education including many extra-curricular activities. I believe that selective education has an important role to play in shaping the future of our young adults. Educated in Cardigan in West Wales, I am an economics graduate of the University of Bristol and a chartered accountant. I retired after a career in various finance and operational roles latterly with a multinational financial services company. I have lived in Esher for the last 40 years. My goal is for Tiffin to continue to be outstanding in every way and to be well positioned to meet the changes that the future will bring.
I am Co Vice Chair of the Governing Board, Chair of the Resources Committee, Chair of the Pay Committee and Chair of the Head’s Performance Review Group.
I was born and educated in Surbiton and now live in Teddington with my husband Simon. I graduated in law and qualified as a solicitor working in the City where I practised commercial litigation for 11 years. I now focus on my role as a school governor and a volunteer on the Cruse Bereavement Helpline. I have three sons who all attended Tiffin School from Year 7. I have seen first-hand how the excellent academic education and exceptionally wide-ranging extracurricular opportunities Tiffin provides benefitted my sons and their peers. I am committed to supporting Tiffin to continue to maintain these high standards for future generations of students. I have considerable experience as a school governor, having been a Parent Governor at the local infant and junior schools my sons attended. I was appointed a Parent Governor at Tiffin in 2013 and I am now a Foundation Governor.
I am a member of the Education Committee and I hold the following Link Governor roles: Oversight of Safeguarding, Looked After Children, Filtering & Monitoring, Allergy Safety, SEND. I am delighted to be able to continue to contribute to the continued success of Tiffin School.
Both my sons attended the school and for several years I was a member of the TPA. Subsequently, I became a Parent Governor and then a Foundation Governor. I am a chartered accountant and have extensive experience in contracts and procurement in the public sector. In addition, I was an external examiner and distance learning tutor at Durham University Business School for over 20 years. In 2009 I was awarded an MBE for services to equality and diversity. I have always strongly supported the school ethos and have enjoyed my long association with the governing board. I have been closely involved with the building of the Sports Hall and its recent extension, and the Learning Resources Centre and kitchen and dining facilities.
I am a member of the Resources Committee, the Pay Committee and the Head’s Performance Review Group. I am also a Link Governor for Health & Safety.
Tiffin changed my life. It gave the son of an immigrant single mother a fair shot of success by cultivating curiosity and instilling confidence from an early age. I made my best friends for life at Tiffin. I am currently a senior director at Flagship Pioneering, the $3B+ venture capital fund most known for starting Moderna. I am responsible for coordinating the development, launch, and management of Flagship’s efforts to originate and grow a new generation of companies aimed at pre-empting, predicting, and preventing novel pathogens and chronic diseases.
Before joining Flagship, I served as an Innovation Fellow at Imperial College’s Institute of Global Health Innovation (2019 to 2021) and as an advisor to Lord Darzi. There I co-led the programme management office for REACT, one of the largest COVID-19 surveillance programmes in the UK, enabling the deployment of over 3 million tests to inform UK government policy. Earlier I led the analytics for Lord Darzi’s 2018 review of health and care, which underpinned the case for an additional £20bn a year of NHS funding. I spent my early career as an analyst at Oliver Wyman, a management consulting firm, and at HgCapital, a European private equity firm. I graduated from Harvard College with an AB in cognitive science (2001 to 2005).
I hope that by serving as a governor I can support the school in its mission to become a truly world class educational institution, and that I can help today’s exceptional students take giant leaps in the future. I am a longstanding Surbiton resident, the lucky husband of Shanika and the proud father of two young children.
I am a member of the Resources Committee, a member of the Admissions Committee and Link Governor for Disadvantaged Students.
I have known Kingston as a child, a student (at the then polytechnic) and for the last 40 or so years as a resident. I have four sons who have all attended Tiffin, the youngest in the 6th form only, and have seen the school develop from an excellent grammar school to a leading school in teaching and learning. I studied mechanical engineering and worked for 14 years in research and development and project work. I then retrained as a teacher and taught in inner London schools for 27 years. With my sons following different interests throughout their school careers, I took the role as coordinator for Tiffin car boot sales for many years. This enabled me to help all the various groups in which my sons were involved and support the extracurricular activities that make Tiffin the school it is. I became a Parent Governor in 1994 and I am now a Foundation Governor.
I am a member of the Education Committee and the Admissions Committee.

The Tiffin School Foundation
The Tiffin School Foundation (Foundation) is a registered charity which owns the school land in Kingston (as trustee) and owns the sports grounds and facilities at Grists. The Foundation has an important role in the governance of Tiffin School. Its charitable objects include the provision and conduct of Tiffin School and the provision of sports and recreation facilities to the local community and Tiffin alumni sports clubs. The Foundation is the principal charitable conduit for parental and alumni donations to the Tiffin Education Fund and other fundraising and legacies that are essential for the School to be able to continue to offer modern facilities and wide extracurricular opportunities to its students. Its role in the governance of the School is explained in more detail here.
The Foundation’s recent activities have included project fundraising and launching a legacy initiative “The 1638 Society”. Approval for two major projects was granted to improve the facilities at the School. Construction has started in Kingston for the provision of a second artificial all-weather pitch, new netball court, upgraded cricket nets and a new long jump. These will be enjoyed by many generations of Tiffinians to come and will be completed by the spring of the 2025-26 academic year. These Kingston facilities are very much needed due to the impact that poor weather often has on the School’s ability to use Grists as well as the revenue generated from evening and weekend third party community lets. This project has been possible due to a single very large donation by an alumnus and the strong support of current parents. The second project for a major, and long overdue, upgrade to our staff room and reception area has been completed over the summer and has been particularly helped by a large legacy from a late teacher. The Foundation, with the support of current parents, has also supported much needed improvements to the School’s Harper Pavilion at Grists over the summer of 2025. The Trustees heartfelt thanks go to all parents and Tiffin alumni and others who have supported the fundraising for these improvements.
In the summer of 2025, the Foundation continued its initiative of providing 11+ familiarisation tests for Year 5 pupils (girls and boys) in the local community who are wanting to experience an entrance test to any school at age 11. The tests are given free to children who are eligible for Pupil Premium and who participate in the School’s Shaping Future’s programme.
